anchors.quote: there's just many many more variables to establish early as well both for the candidate and for the recruiter

the screening call was where I try tried to remove any kind of ambiguity that might exist so I think it's important early that a recruiter understands not only whether the candidate can do the job but whether the practical route to employing them is actually possible

claim_en: With overseas candidates the recruiter used the screening call to settle early the practical variables (right to work, sponsorship, salary, relocation, time zone, payroll, background checks), checking not only whether the candidate can do the job but whether employing them is possible.

anchors.quote: sponsorship is probably the hardest practical barrier to overcome because not every company would would have that facility to sponsor

claim_en: Sponsorship is probably the hardest practical barrier for overseas candidates, because not every company can sponsor.

anchors.quote: if somebody already has the right to work for an existing visa uh the conversation is is way way easier if they depend entirely on the employer sponsoring them number of available organizations shrinks massively

claim_en: A candidate who already has the right to work through an existing visa has a much easier conversation; one who depends entirely on employer sponsorship faces a massively smaller set of employers.

anchors.quote: in the UK the skilled worker route requires an employer to sponsor an eligible role and then fulfill the sponsorship duties that are associated with that specific role

claim_en: In the UK the skilled worker route requires an employer to sponsor an eligible role and fulfill the sponsorship duties for it.

anchors.quote: probably not on the CV um because then that introduces bias in the whole selection process
whereas if you put it on your CV um it gives people a reason to to click past

claim_en: Do not mention needing sponsorship on the CV: it introduces bias into the selection process and gives people a reason to click past.

anchors.quote: I would say you need to mention it early though
it should be clear on the application or during the first recruiter conversation
hiding it until the final interview just wastes everybody's time

claim_en: Mention the need for sponsorship early, on the application or in the first recruiter conversation; hiding it until the final interview wastes everyone's time and undermines trust.

anchors.quote: explain your position accurately but confidently as well what permissions you currently have when it expires is a big one that you need to remember and then exactly what support you would need

claim_en: Explain the visa position accurately and confidently: the permissions currently held, when they expire and exactly what support would be needed.

anchors.quote: the reality unfortunately is that candidates are probably going to encounter practical obstacles so sponsorship relocation financial or security processes employers that are just cautious about that particular region

claim_en: Candidates from some regions are likely to meet practical obstacles: sponsorship, relocation, financial or security processes, and employers cautious about that region.

anchors.quote: your availability focus on internationally minded employers
target companies that can realistically hire you

claim_en: International candidates should focus on internationally minded employers that can realistically hire them.

anchors.quote: build relationships with people that can actually see your ability before they see any kind of administration complication
build relationships rather than relying exclusively on applications

claim_en: Build relationships through networking with people who can see the candidate's ability before any administrative complication, rather than relying only on applications.

anchors.quote: i think sometimes but uh usually because of the employer's operating constraints rather than the engineers talent

claim_en: A candidate's current country sometimes matters, usually because of the employer's operating constraints (regulated data that must stay in the country, time zone, legal entities, payroll, security) rather than the engineer's talent.

anchors.quote: what matters commercially is often a combination of specialist skills autonomy availability location and cost rather than the location itself

claim_en: For the recruiter's company, what matters commercially is often a combination of specialist skills, autonomy, availability, location and cost rather than the location itself.

anchors.quote: I think it's a good question for candidates to ask and show that they're bought into the process like is my location a hard restriction or is there a practical concern that I can help you address

claim_en: Candidates should ask whether their location is a hard restriction or a practical concern they can help address; it shows they are bought into the process.

anchors.quote: improve your LinkedIn profile show that you're active rather than invisible
there's nothing worse than coming across a LinkedIn profile and there's no picture there's like one job history mentioned on there but there's no bio

claim_en: Improve the LinkedIn profile and show activity; a profile with no picture, a single job, no bio and no comments or posts is the worst thing to come across.

anchors.quote: that's not me telling you to go post AI slop on LinkedIn please don't do that don't use an NLM or an AI tool to start posting about something that you haven't written

claim_en: Being active on LinkedIn does not mean posting AI generated content the candidate has not written.

anchors.quote: if you're searchable and if you're accessible online that makes you much more of a um approachable candidate

claim_en: Being searchable and accessible online makes a candidate much more approachable.
